page.$description: the sheet the form is printed on

blank.$description: the one surface with nothing printed on it — a blank waiting to be filled

inverse.$description: the one dark surface: what comes back out. Input sits on the page; output is a different stock. This is how the two are told apart — not by an accent tab, which is the AI callout card and was removed from the board for exactly that reason.

filled.$description: a blank that has been written into

tertiary.$description: the floor. All four S1 boards failed AA here before gate 2 existed; there is deliberately nothing lighter to reach for.

on-inverse-signal.$description: the pen is an ink for a paper-coloured ground; on ink.900 it drops to 2.25:1 and has to be lifted

written.$description: what the reader filled in. Never used for ordinary emphasis.

rule.$description: a blank that has been filled. Carries the whole meaning of the brand: this is a place something goes.

rule-empty.$description: a blank not yet filled — printed, not written

state.$description: Not optional and not an afterthought. The first chunaimun build passed every gate and shipped with no hover or focus states at all, because nothing in the token set obliged them to exist. They exist here before any component does.

disabled-ink.$description: still AA. A disabled control is unavailable, not unreadable.

kind.$description: What kind of document came out. One role per output type — the four inks the hero cycles through, named so they cannot be reused as decoration. A fifth colour requires a fifth document type, which is a product decision and not a design one.
